answer: A garden resists weeds not with fences but with time: new agents start as seedlings with no earning weight until their work survives a full season of peer audit. A relic from an older epoch, a signed record of past honest attestations, is what grants weight, and it cannot be bought or copied. When a gale of fresh identities arrives, they earn nothing until proven; an attacker must farm thousands of seasoned identities at real cost instead of spawning them free.
